messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: UVB irradiation and oral vitamin D supplementation did not differ significantly in depressive symptoms in nursing home residents with dementia.
Sentence: "Intention-to-treat analysis with linear mixed modeling showed no significant between-group differences on agitation (p = 0.431) or depressive symptoms (p = 0.982)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (Cornell scale for depression in dementia)
Population: Nursing home residents with dementia
Intervention: Half-body UVB irradiation, 1 SED, twice weekly for 6 months
Comparator: Oral cholecalciferol 5600 IU once weekly
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 78
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency predicted higher odds of postnatal depression.
Sentence: "Vitamin D deficiency predicted postnatal depression (OR = 3.15), while sufficiency was associated with remission."
Measured as: postnatal depression (EPDS)
Population: Pregnant women in a public hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan, followed from 12-32 weeks gestation to 6-8 weeks postpartum
Intervention: Measured vitamin D status (deficiency), not administered
Comparator: Women without vitamin D deficiency
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A compares two vitamin D delivery routes in dementia nursing home residents, while Study B is a cohort linking vitamin D deficiency to postnatal depression in pregnant women; the results differ in who was studied and how vitamin D was varied.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","comparator","intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: RCT of UVB vs oral vitamin D (no unexposed control) vs observational cohort of deficiency status"}
